content:
incident-bot: PAGER — SEV2 elevated 5xx rate detected on production inference endpoint /v1/generate. Alert id=ALRT-20260314-9b2. Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/kv-prefix-cache-elevations.

sam_lee: oncall ack — investigating. noticed 5xx spike starting ~1782102500, currently ~18% errors over 5m window, p95 latency up 2.4x. Error classes: 502 gateway, 504 upstream timeout, and a few 500s with "invalid KV payload".

sam_lee: querying logs now:
```bash
kubectl -n inference logs -l app=inference --since=15m | egrep "prefix-cache|KVError|evict" | tail -n 200
```

sam_lee: sample from logs:
```
[13:02:45] WARN prefix-cache shard=3 miss_count=4230 eviction_count=1200 err="corrupted-payload" request_id=rid-9af3
[13:02:46] ERROR kv.client shard=3 code=E_PAYLOAD_CORRUPT desc="kv decode failed" stack=... request_id=rid-9af4
[13:03:01] WARN gateway request_id=rid-9f2 timed out after 30s upstream=cache-3
```

marta_p: confirming from KV team side — shard-3 showing increased CRC/deserialize failures. Noticed a GC/planned rolling compaction on the backing store ~12:58 which lines up. Eviction rate on prefix cache skyrocketed and we see many cache misses forwarded to slow store causing timeouts.

ops_lead: metrics: prefix_cache.evictions_per_min increased 115x on nodes in us-west-2a; cpu of cache workers spiked to 96%. This looks like an eviction storm + corrupt payloads causing retries into the slow path.

sam_lee: proposed immediate mitigations (canary then roll):
- disable prefix-cache reads on edge (fallback to direct store/model read) to avoid corrupted cached payloads.
- avoid mass restarts; use graceful flush on affected shards.
- temporarily bump retry/backoff and circuit-breaker thresholds to reduce request amplification.

sam_lee: toggling feature flag for prefix-cache reads to OFF for 25% of edge nodes (canary):
```bash
curl -X POST https://configsvc.internal/api/v1/flags/prefix_cache_reads -d '{"state":"off","scope":"edge","percent":25}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

sam_lee: canary applied at 13:05. Monitoring dashboard: https://telemetry/alerts/ALRT-20260314-9b2 (live).

julia-cs: CS note — two enterprise customers reported failed calls and one custom integration retried aggressively and hit rate limits. They're asking for ETA and whether feature flags affect their Dedicated deployment.

sam_lee: CS: Dedicated customers not affected by hosted feature toggle. ETA: canary -> 50% in 10m if metrics look good, full rollout 30–45m. Sending interim status to affected accounts.

ryan_sre: I can flush shard-3's in-memory prefix cache but we must avoid a thundering herd. Runbook suggests graceful shard flush endpoint.

ops_lead: yes, do not `kill` processes. Use internal flush endpoint that drains active requests then clears cache: POST /internal/cache/flush?shard=3&grace=true. Example: 
```bash
curl -X POST "https://inference-internal.us-west-2/cache/flush?shard=3&grace=true" -H "X-Req-ID: flush-1782102567"
```

ryan_sre: initiated graceful flush on shard-3 at 13:12. Observed cache size drop from 48GB -> 2GB on that shard and eviction rate normalized.

sam_lee: after flush + canary toggle -> 5xx rate dropped from 18% -> 3.2% on canary nodes, overall cluster 5xx is down to 7.5%. Moving to 50% rollout now.

incident-bot: Incident doc created: https://redwood/incidents/1782102567. Severity SEV2. Pager updated and oncall rotations notified.

sam_lee: rolling toggle to 50% at 13:22. Observing: p95 latency returning to baseline, error budget burn halted. Will keep traffic on fallback path until we confirm backend store integrity.

marta_p: KV team is preserving logs and snapshots for shard-3. We suspect a bad compaction/generation that corrupted a subset of entries. Next steps: snapshot restore test on staging, replay recent writes, and audit compaction job.

julia-cs: sent customer update: "We're aware of elevated errors impacting some requests. Mitigation in place, requests are routing around affected cache entries. We'll follow up with a postmortem once root cause verified." :white_check_mark:

sam_lee: handoff: @nate will take the incident for the next 30–60m to monitor rollout, coordinate KV deeper triage, and drive postmortem. My notes: preserved heap/profile of affected process (pid 2348), captured core dump, retained logs: s3://redwood-incidents/1782102567/trace.tar.gz.

nate: taking over — will keep watch on rollback thresholds and coordinate with infra to block the compaction job until we have a fix. Adding follow-ups: reproduce corruption locally, add checksum verification at cache load, and add alert to detect sudden eviction spikes.

incident-bot: Reminder: schedule postmortem meeting in 24h and assign owners for RCA.

nate: ack — continuing monitoring and will post next update in 30m.
